collection.title: Fine-tuning an intracellular allosteric pocket programs GPCR signaling bias
collection.authors: Shi, X.; Zhu, R.; Chang, K.; Yu, P.; Yuan, Q.; Zhang, Y.; Lu, X.; Zhou, Z.; Zhu, C.; Lan, X.; Li, M.; Li, R.; Qiao, X.; Xie, W.; Zhuang, Y.; Xu, H. E.; Yin, W.; Zhao, M.; Zhang, J.
collection.author_corresponding_institution: School of Medicine, Shanghai Jiao Tong University
collection.abstract: Biased signaling of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) offers a route for precise therapeutics with fewer adverse effects. Intracellular allosteric ligands can impose such bias, yet how subtle chemical changes within these pockets reshape receptor-transducer coupling and downstream signaling remains unclear. Here, we systematically fine-tuned the intracellular allosteric pocket of neurotensin receptor 1 (NTSR1) through chemical modification of the {beta}-arrestin-biased ligand SBI-553. Minor changes to the ligand scaffold altered transducer-coupling preferences, generating distinct profiles of G-protein and {beta}-arrestin signaling. Cryo-electron microscopy structures of NTSR1-{beta}-arrestin2 complexes bound to designed allosteric probes revealed ligand-dependent remodeling of the intracellular cavity that reshapes the receptor-effector interface. Alanine scanning identified transducer-sensitive residues within and beyond the immediate ligand-contact region. In mice, SBI-553 and N065 produced distinct physiological profiles, with N065 improving survival in a lethal endotoxemia model. Finally, phosphoproteomic profiling revealed partially overlapping but distinct downstream signaling profiles among the three modulators. Together, these findings establish the intracellular allosteric pocket as a tunable determinant of transducer coupling and show that closely related modulators can generate distinct signaling and physiological profiles.
